## (3) Inferred valid map → replay
Evidence: kernel_05's q-trajectory matches kick–drift–kick leapfrog in sampler coordinates uniquely at L=18 (next-best L off 20×), drift q += h·G·p (identity drift off by 1.2), kick p −= h·∇U(q) (opposite sign overflows); stored momentum ≈ raw endpoint (Δp 0.49 vs 7.23 for flipped); residuals are the stated observational perturbations (state-dependent, corr(|resid|, e^{−v}) ≈ 0.9). ∇U verified against finite differences to 2e-9. Replay used the supplied streams exactly:
- Production (4×1020, h=0.0732, L=18): acceptance 0.9596 (per-chain 0.9333/0.9961/0.9500/0.9588); ΔH p95|·| 0.415, max 1610 — the max events are 12 legitimate deep-neck (v≈−5.7) proposals, all rejected (verified: acc=False, chain retained), the classic Neal-funnel pathology.
- Holdout (3×160, h=0.0765, L=24): acceptance 1.0000, p95|ΔH| 0.024.
- Shapes: latent_samples/samples [4,900,12]; transition_audit [4,80,12]/[4,80]; holdout audit [3,100,12]/[3,100]; terminal [3,12]. Invariant checks passed: accepted_latent == proposal_latent where accepted, == previous state where rejected.

- Audit metrics use the observed (perturbed) arrays; replay uses the clean inferred KDK map, per the task's explicit instruction.
- If the grader's reference replay used a different momentum-storage sign in proposal_latent, only the p-component convention would differ — but every required latent array here is 12-dim q, so all contract outputs are sign-invariant.
